facts.claim: Dendrites receive input at synapses
facts.quote: receive information from other neurons at specialized areas of contact called synapses.
facts.note: WebFetch summarizer output; quote may be elided, re-verify on page

facts.claim: Soma is the cell body
facts.quote: the main part of a neuron is the cell body, which is also known as the soma

facts.claim: Axon hillock is where axon emerges from soma
facts.quote: Where the axon emerges from the cell body, there is a special region referred to as the axon hillock.

facts.claim: Axon carries the nerve impulse to targets
facts.quote: a fiber that emerges from the cell body and projects to target cells

facts.claim: Myelin is made from glial cells; gaps are nodes of Ranvier
facts.quote: Each gap is called a node of Ranvier and is important to the way that electrical signals travel down the axon.
facts.note: myelin quote: an insulating substance called myelin, which is actually made from glial cells.

facts.claim: Axon terminal at axon end, usually branched
facts.quote: At the end of the axon is the axon terminal, where there are usually several branches extending toward the target cell.

facts.claim: Multipolar: one axon, two or more dendrites
facts.quote: have one axon and two or more dendrites (usually many more).

facts.claim: Bipolar: two processes from opposite ends
facts.quote: have two processes, which extend from each end of the cell body, opposite to each other.

facts.claim: Human unipolar cells are pseudo-unipolar; sensory
facts.quote: the unipolar cells in humans are more appropriately called 'pseudo-unipolar' cells.
facts.note: also: Unipolar cells are exclusively sensory neurons.

facts.claim: Sensory/motor/interneuron definitions
facts.note: Not found on 12.1 or 12.2 via fetch (only unipolar=sensory)

facts.claim: Astrocytes maintain extracellular chemistry, clear signaling molecules, blood-brain barrier
facts.quote: maintaining the concentration of chemicals in the extracellular space, removing excess signaling molecules
facts.note: K+ buffering / glutamate uptake not named

facts.claim: Oligodendrocyte myelinates multiple axon segments
facts.quote: One oligodendrocyte will provide the myelin for multiple axon segments, either for the same axon or for separate axons.

facts.claim: Microglia are CNS-resident macrophages
facts.quote: referred to as CNS-resident macrophages.

facts.claim: Ependymal cells make CSF
facts.quote: filters blood to make cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), the fluid that circulates through the CNS.

facts.claim: Schwann cell myelinates one axon segment
facts.quote: a Schwann cell wraps around a portion of only one axon segment.

facts.claim: Satellite cells surround neuron cell bodies, astrocyte-like support
facts.quote: surround the cell bodies of neurons
facts.note: also: performing similar functions in the periphery as astrocytes do in the CNS

facts.claim: AP opens voltage-gated Ca2+ channels
facts.quote: When an action potential reaches the axon terminals, voltage-gated Ca2+ channels in the membrane of the synaptic end bulb open.

facts.claim: Ca2+ drives vesicle fusion; exocytosis into cleft
facts.quote: The neurotransmitter is released through exocytosis into the small gap between the cells, known as the synaptic cleft.
facts.note: SNARE not named on page; Europe PMC record PMC12325603 (Bera 2025, CC BY-NC-ND) abstract mentions SNARE assembly for docking/priming

facts.claim: Neurotransmitter binds receptors; cleared by degradation or reuptake
facts.quote: The neurotransmitter is cleared from the synapse either by enzymatic degradation, neuronal reuptake, or glial reuptake.
facts.note: EPSP/IPSP terms not confirmed in fetched extract

facts.claim: Central synapse cleft ~20 nm
facts.quote: Typically, at the central synapses, cleft width is ~20nm
facts.note: BioNumbers secondary compilation (cites Kandel 2000, Barberis 2011); license unspecified; not on OpenStax

facts.claim: Glutamate excitatory
facts.quote: Glutamate is considered an excitatory amino acid

facts.claim: GABA inhibitory
facts.quote: GABA are considered inhibitory amino acids, again because their receptors cause hyperpolarization.

facts.claim: ACh depolarizes via nicotinic receptor
facts.quote: When acetylcholine binds to the nicotinic receptor, the postsynaptic cell is depolarized.

facts.claim: Serotonin made from tryptophan; dopamine and norepinephrine have own systems
facts.quote: Serotonin is made from tryptophan.
facts.note: Also: Dopamine is part of its own system, the dopaminergic system; Norepinephrine and epinephrine belong to the adrenergic neurotransmitter system.

facts.topic: synaptic delay / vesicle size / synapse count
facts.claim: delay ~0.5 ms, vesicle ~40 nm, 1e14 synapses
Ionotropic = ligand-gated channels; metabotropic = metabolic changes
facts.quote: A metabotropic receptor involves a complex of proteins that result in metabolic changes within the cell.

facts.claim: Mg2+ blocks NMDA currents voltage-dependently
facts.quote: At negative membrane potentials Mg2+ caused a previously characterized voltage-dependent block of inward NMDA-activated currents.

facts.claim: Hippocampal Hebbian LTP needs Ca2+ influx via NMDA receptor channels
facts.quote: calcium influx through voltage-dependent NMDA receptor channels
facts.note: Gustafsson 2026, Hippocampus, PMC13439494, CC BY; abstract fragment only via Europe PMC search

facts.claim: MS: immune system attacks myelin
facts.quote: In MS, the immune system attacks myelin.
facts.note: OpenStax 12.2 also: autoimmune, destruction of myelin in the CNS
